Erin —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the sample counts. Short answer: Redwood bills based on the model-level token stream (the tokens produced/consumed by the model on the request), not a normalized canonical token definition. So differences between SentencePiece and BPE will show up in billed token counts.

Longer explanation and options below:

- Billing basis: per-token for input+output per model variant. We record tokens as whatever the tokenizer paired to the served model emits.
- Why it matters: models with more aggressive subword splitting (common with SentencePiece variants) will show higher token counts on the same UTF-8 text. That is consistent across most inference providers.
- Mitigations we offer:
  * Model selection guidance — we can benchmark your corpora across candidate models and recommend the best token-efficiency / quality tradeoff.
  * Pricing concession approach — for multi-model deployments we can create an \"equivalent-token\" baseline so you don't get penalized during evaluation/final billing.
  * Pre-tokenization cache — for repeated prompts we can cache the tokenized prefixes and reduce billed input-side tokens in practice.

I'm attaching our standard hosted rate card (PDF) and a short note that shows how your CSV maps into billed tokens for a BPE vs SentencePiece model.

Proposed next steps: 1) I can run a quick 1k-sample benchmark across 3 model candidates and return estimated monthly delta; 2) Marissa can model a discount schedule for blended usage if you expect sustained volume.

Would you like me to proceed with #1? If yes, I'll need a signed evaluation SOW (we can keep it minimal) or confirmation to proceed under the trial terms.

Thanks —
